cells.quote: Operation time: Cumulative average operation time increased temporarily (slope = 7.61, p < 0.001), reflecting the added challenges of major resections.
cells.note: Observational comparison of learning phases; phase 2 included a transition to major resections, so the contrast is confounded by case complexity.

cells.quote: Operation time: Cumulative average operation time began to decrease significantly (slope = − 0.50, p < 0.001), demonstrating growing efficiency despite case complexity.
cells.note: Lower operation time in the early-mastery phase is interpreted as improved efficiency; this is a nonrandomized phase comparison.

cells.quote: Operation time: Cumulative average operation time stabilized, with no significant changes observed (slope = − 0.04, p = 0.331).
cells.note: The nonsignificant result does not establish equivalence; it is consistent with the authors’ interpretation of performance stabilization.

cells.quote: Notably, 8 (88.9%) out of 9 conversions occurred before the 66th procedure, spanning the Competency, Proficiency, and Early Mastery phases. In the Full Mastery phase (Cases 66–100), only one conversion was observed.
cells.note: The study reports a descriptive decline in conversions after case 65, but does not provide an inferential effect estimate for this contrast.
